controlled_gap_explanation.observed_pattern_under_review: SYS-12 attempt02: sampled_b_hub_desired_revision=1573 vs b_db_after_sync=1575 (unexplained 2-unit difference)
controlled_gap_explanation.reproduction: exactly 2 owned hub-side changes (script-2 + task-2) were made while the agent container was stopped; the hub revision_sequence advanced by >=2 while the agent local revision stayed frozen, and after reconnect the agent caught up
controlled_gap_explanation.hub_watermark_semantics: revision_sequence is a single monotonic hub watermark advanced by EVERY hub-side object change (any batch); the agent local sync_state.global_revision is the watermark value delivered in its last SYNC response, and the hub node row is the value the agent last reported back (heartbeat cadence ~30s, revision_check ~45s)
controlled_gap_explanation.conclusion: the 1573 vs 1575 pattern is a sampling-order artifact of a monotonic global watermark: the hub-side sample was taken 2 changes earlier than the agent-side read, so the agent value being HIGHER means the agent had already applied the newer watermark (no loss, no unapplied state); after convergence the hub row reports the agent applied revision and sync_status=synced, and every object matches per-revision+sha
